say: A first look at the new tracker. What it was, what it is now, and what it asks of you.
This is what the tracker was.
Four blocks, fixed by the clock. Eight to ten. Ten to twelve. The same four for everyone, whatever the work was.
cap:
Four blocks.
Fixed by the clock.

say: Your Salesforce numbers were typed by hand. Closed. Overdue. Guessed at four o'clock, from memory.
It counted whether a box was filled. It could not see whether the work moved.
This is what it is now. Sign in before ten and the day is already laid out. Your book is read from Salesforce before you arrive.
cap:
The day is already
laid out.

say: Every kind of work shows how much of it there is. Yours, and the branch's.
cap:
How much there is.
Yours, and the branch's.

say: And how much of it actually needs you. A task worked yesterday is in hand. One untouched for three weeks is not.
cap:
How much of it
needs you.

say: Tick the block, and the work itself appears. Not a count. The tasks.
cap:
The work itself.
Not a count.

say: Three for one agent is one conversation, not three.
cap:
Three for one agent
is one conversation.

say: The block is sized against your own pace. What you actually clear in a day, from your own last sixty days. It shows its working.
If the work will not fill two hours, it says so. Half an hour of licensing does not need a block of its own.
cap:
If it will not fill two hours,
it says so.

say: Late work is grouped by the agent it is for.
Your task position is live. Closed. Open. Overdue. Nobody types a number again.
An overdue task with no reason gets a box. What you write there goes straight into Salesforce.
When the block ends, one question. Did it land.
What is required of you is three things.
Tick what the block is for. Work the list. Answer the question at the close.
cap:
Tick the block.
Work the list.
Answer at the close.

say: Nothing is retyped. Salesforce already holds what you did. The tracker only asks whether it landed.
sub:
Salesforce already holds what you did.
The tracker asks whether it landed.

say: This is where it is going.
